The half-width of the CME is based on later imagery in STEREO A COR2, as in coronagraphs there is/are later, wider, lobe(s) of this CME that seem to be integral part of it.

CME first seen to the North by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-02T03:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 in later frames. This event is blocked by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is a C1.8 flare from Active Region 14455 (N15E09) seen peaking at 2026-06-02T02:50Z in SDO AIA 131. A small jet of filament ejecta is visible in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304 in association with this flare, and is heavily deflected to the North, likely due to this region sitting just North of a coronal hole.

This event is blocked by the pylon in GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is a C3.1 flare from Active Region 14455 (N15E01) which peaked at 2026-06-02T06:59Z as seen in SDO AIA 131. A small jet of filament ejecta is visible in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304 in association with this flare, and is heavily deflected to the North, likely due to this region sitting just North of a coronal hole.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Bright loop CME first seen to the East by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-02T12:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME has a faint, diffuse, preceding feature, but not a shock, seen ahead of the main bulk, likely due to the nature of the source eruption. The source of this event is a very gradual filament eruption seen centered at approx. S10E75 as seen in GOES SUVI, STEREO A EUVI and SDO AIA 304. This filament becomes unstable beginning at approx. 2026-06-02T10:30Z and gradually rises off the limb, but does not begin to disconnect from the disk until approx. 2026-06-02T12:00Z. This earlier rise likely accounts for the diffuse feature seen in coronagraphs before the main bulk of the filament ejecta. Field line opening, dimming and post eruptive arcades are also visible in association with this eruption in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Bright CME first seen to the Northeast by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-02T17:00Z. The source of this event is a filament eruption seen along or just beyond the NE limb at approx. N18 as seen in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-06-02T16:43Z. Wide opening field lines are also visible in association with this eruption in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement of the BULK feature based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 as well as on the visible source over the NE limb.

data.note: CME first seen to the East in STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-06-02T17:23Z. The CME is not clearly seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 as it is likely obscured by the occulting disk. The source of this event is an M3.3 class flare from Active Region 14455 (N13W05) which peaked at 2026-06-02T16:50Z as seen in SDO AIA 131. Opening field lines and dimming are also observed in association with this flare in SDO AIA 171, 193 and 211 with the dimming and opening facing Southward, likely indicating some Southern deflection.

cmeAnalyses.note: Very speculative measurement based on limited frames from STEREO A COR2 and visible on-disk source.

data.note: Narrow, faint CME first seen to the NE in STEREO A COR2 starting around 2026-06-02T18:09Z. This feature is only seen in STEREO A COR2 because it is mostly likely obscured by the occulting disk in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is most likely some additional outflow following CME: 2026-06-02T17:23Z as there is no independent source signature apart from continuous field line fluctuation following CME: 2026-06-02T17:23Z. This CME fades before reached the end of the FOV of STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative measurement based on limited imagery from STEREO A COR2 and approximate source location.

data.note: CME first seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-06-02T19:48Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is covered by a real-time data gap in STEREO A COR2. There are two source candidates for this CME. The first and most likely is some faint field line movement from beyond the NE limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning around 2026-06-02T17:30Z following the filament eruption associated with CME: 2026-06-02T17:00Z. The second and less likely candidate is some additional minor ejecta from AR 14455 following CME: 2026-06-02T17:23Z, but measurement indicates that this second source candidate is not a good fit.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement due to lack of available triangulation and uncertain source.

data.note: Narrow CME first visible to the NE part way into the FOV of SOHO LASCO C2 staring around 2026-06-02T23:00Z. It is also seen to the NE in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is covered by a real-time data gap in STEREO A COR2. No source candidate has been found on the Earth-facing disk, so the source is most likely far-sided. This front could be additional outflow following CME: 2026-06-02T17:00Z.

It is also seen as a halo to the NW in GOES CCOR-1. This CME is associated with an M9.3 class flare from AR 14455 (N13W10) that peaked at 2026-06-03T01:36Z. The flare can best be seen in SDO AIA 131.

data.note: This CME is visible as a partial halo to the north/northwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery, and to the northeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is an M7.7 flare from Active Region 14455 (N14W13) starting around 2026-06-03T07:00Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/194/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304 imagery, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. A large ejecta is associated with this event which is deflected to the northwest. Additionally, an EUV wave is observed moving northwest of the eruption site, as seen in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195/284 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Approximate analysis of the messy, two-lobed bulk front of this CME, based on the fit with three coronagraphs (STEREO A COR2, SOHO LASCO and GOES CCOR-1). There is clear northward deflection from the source location of the M-class flare (N14W13) but the associated erupting filament seems to originate a bit to the west from the flare location and is then seen deflecting northwardly, so the coronal signatures generally confirm this analysis. The half-width of the CME is based on later imagery in STEREO A COR2, as in coronagraphs there is/are later, wider, lobe(s) of this CME that seem to be integral part of it.

The source is an X1.0 flare and subsequent eruption from Active Region 14455 (N14W16) starting around 2026-06-03T11:20Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. The associated ejecta displays a southeast deflection as seen in SDO AIA 304 imagery. A faint EUV wave is observed moving northwest of the eruption site, however, in SDO AIA 193 imagery.

data.note: Far-sided halo CME to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and wide front observed to the W in STEREO A COR2. The source is far-sided from Earth and likely STEREO A (W59.9) as well, should be well observed by Solar Orbiter (E156.3) when its data is available. The source is more directly observed in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 on or beyond STEREO's limb (~W149.9) as a filament eruption and field line movement starting around 2026-06-05T08:15Z. It is also observed in GOES SUVI 195/284, and less prominent in SDO AIA 171/193/211 with its closer field-of-view, as wide opening field lines and EUV wave over the SE limb starting around 2026-06-05T09:00Z. Latest Solar Orbiter EUI 304 imagery at 2026-06-0500:01Z shows numerous filaments resting around the W180-E150 and N15-S30 range surrounding former Active Regions 14439 and 14442, for potential candidates. Likely associated with an estimated M3 [M2,M6] flare observed by Solar Orbiter STIX peaking at 2026-06-05T08:58Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A plane-of-sky taken at W149.9, with STEREO A currently located at W59.9.

data.note: Faint CME front observed to the NE only in STEREO A COR2. No clear source for this CME is observed in SDO AIA, GOES SUVI, or STEREO A EUVI.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A plane-of-sky taken at E30.1, with STEREO A currently located at W59.9.

data.note: Faint CME to the NW in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1, and NE in STEREO A COR2, pylon obscured in LASCO C3. The source is a C4.1 flare from AR 14455 which peaked at 2026-06-05T15:03Z observed in SDO AIA 131, also observed as field line movement and small dimming in SDO AIA 171/193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. The CME appears deflected northward and tracks askew with the swpc_cat tool, as such the parameters could vary slightly, with high confidence in the out-of-ecliptic direction.

data.note: Narrow CME first seen to the ne by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-06-05T16:09Z. This CME is either directed into the pylon or occulting disk in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, and is therefore not clearly visible. There is no clear source that fits the CME seen for this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A plane-of-sky measurement using a longitude of E30.1 (as STEREO A is currently located at W59.9) due to lack of clear source an coronagraph imagery to triangulate.

data.note: CME first seen to the SW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-05T23:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-06-05T19:09Z. The source of this event is field line opening seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA 171 beginning at 2026-06-05T22:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using a longitude of W90 due to source location near the limb and lack of SOHO/GOES coronagraph imagery to triangulate.

data.note: This CME is visible to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery. The source is likely far-sided as there are no source signatures on the Earth-facing disk around the time of this event.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was made using a longitude of -90 degrees due to the far-sided and therefore unknown source location.

data.note: This CME is visible to the north in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and to the northeast in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is unknown, but may be related to faint field line movement visible over the northeast limb in SDO AIA 171 starting around 2026-06-06T03:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible to the southwest in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is a far-sided eruption visible on the southwest limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 imagery starting around 2026-06-06T13:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: This CME is visible as a southeast partial halo in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 imagery, and is seen to the east in STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is an eruption and M1.8 flare from Active Region 14461 (S22E24) starting around 2025-06-06T13:45Z as seen in SDO AIA 131/171/193/304, GOES SUVI 131/171/195/284/304, and STEREO A EUVI 195/304 imagery. An opening of field lines is visible over the southeast limb in STEREO A EUVI 195 imagery, and a large EUV wave and dimming is observed surrounding the eruption site in SDO AIA 193 and GOES SUVI 195/284 imagery. Additionally, post eruptive arcades are visible in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/105 imagery starting around 2026-06-06T15:00Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Updated bulk measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Shock measurement following the outermost faint feature observed in GOES CCOR-1 imagery. A default half-width of 45 degrees was used as the shock feature is not observed in STEREO A COR2 imagery.
Preliminary bulk measurement based on the source longitude.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not seen in STEREO A COR2. The source may be field line movement in SDO AIA starting around 2026-06-06T16:34Z over the E limb around S10, or AR 14464 with slow brightening near S09E63, the movement is not too clear where it traces on-disk.

cmeAnalyses.note: SOHO LASCO C2/C3 3D analysis using E63 as the likely observed source longitude.

data.note: CME observed to the S in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1, not in STEREO A COR2 during a data gap spanning 2026-06-06T19:09Z to 2026-06-06T23:09Z. The source is a filament eruption far-sided from Earth, observed in STEREO A EUVI 304 at 2026-06-06T19:15Z as filament ejecta on/near its west limb, putting it at approximately W150 with STEREO A currently located at W60. Also observed as filament ejecta over the S limb in GOES SUVI 304.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative analysis of the shock front associated with this CME, using only GOES CCOR-1 due to its good view of the shock front and lack of STEREO A COR2 to triangulate with. W150 is used as the approximate source of the observed filament, and the width could greatly vary as well due to the partial halo single spacecraft analysis.

SOHO LASCO C2/C3 only fit due to the lack of STEREO A COR2 visibility to triangulate. W150 is used as the approximate source of the observed filament, and the lat/lon could vary. Higher confidence in the southward deflection out of the ecliptic plane, regardless.

data.note: Bright, relatively narrow CME seen to the southeast in SOHO LASCO C2, C3, and STEREO A COR2A, along with GOES CCOR-1 likely associated with a far-sided eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using all available spacecraft for triangulation of the longitude.

data.note: Narrow CME seen to the southeast seen in STEREO Ahead with seemingly no corresponding match in GOES and SOHO coronagraphs, likely associated with a far-sided eruption relative to the Earth-Sun line.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO Ahead plane of sky with just a few frames.

data.note: Minor CME seen to the northeast in a few frames of STEREO Ahead coronagraphs before it quickly disappears with unknown originating source.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO Ahead plane of sky measurement, as the source is unknown and the CME is not well observed in SOHO or GOES coronagraphs.

data.note: CME characterized by a wide, dark front seen to the west in STEREO Ahead, SOHO, and GOES coronagraphs with unknown source, perhaps in association with eruptive activity taking place over the STEREO Ahead western limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge using three spacecraft (SOHO, STEREO Ahead, GOES) for triangulation of the longitude. High uncertainty in longitude with error in longitude up to +/- 30 degrees.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the South by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-07T19:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This event is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a reduced campaign cadence. The source of this event is faint dimming seen centered at approx. S40E20 beginning at approx. 2026-06-07T18:25Z as seen in SDO AIA 193 and 211.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Faint CME seen to the South by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-07T22:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap which began at 2026-06-07T20:08Z. The source of this event is minor dimming and field line movement seen centered at approx. S40W20 beginning at approx. 2026-06-07T21:30Z as seen in SDO AIA 171, 193 and 211.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASC C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2, and to the SSE in SOHO LASCO C2 and faintly in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is likely on or near STEREO A's SW limb, currently around W150 with STEREO A at W60.2, observed in STEREO A EUVI 304 as filament ejecta starting around 2026-06-08T01:45Z. Although a bright spot on-disk is briefly observed with this filament ejecta on the limb, around W150, triangulation puts the front around E178, so the source is either further around the limb or deflected.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2, even more faintly in SOHO LASCO C3/GOES CCOR-1 due to it fading into the background after early frames. The source is likely an area of field line movement and dimming centered around S08E42, near AR 14464 (S12E35) starting around 2026-06-08T04:25Z in SDO AIA 171/193.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2, noting the poor image quality in STEREO A COR2 due on an ongoing campaign along with the faint leading edge providing some uncertainty.

data.note: CME observed to the SW in STEREO A COR2 and SSW in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source is very likely far-sided from Earth due to triangulation, likely visible in STEREO A EUVI 195/304 at 2026-06-08T07:25Z as field line dimming and movement on or near its SW limb, which is located around W150 with STEREO A at W60.3.

cmeAnalyses.note: Bulk triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and two available frames of STEREO A COR2. Front appears slightly more wide in COR2A than C2/C3.

Shock front triangulation between SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. With the poor image quality in STEREO A COR2 due to a campaign, W162 is used as the bulk longitude source and varying the parameters from there. Tracking the width via CCOR-1's view of the SE/S/SW expanding faint shock front, but the width could vary due to the uncertainty.

data.note: CME first seen to the NW by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-09T07:12Z, but fades before exiting the field-of-view and is therefore not seen in other coronagraphs. The source of this event is field line opening seen from beyond the NNW limb in SDO AIA 171 and GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approx. 2026-06-09T06:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using a longitude of W90 due to source along the limb and lack of imagery for triangulation.

data.note: CME first seen to the West by STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-06-09T09:08Z. This CME is not seen by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 or GOES CCOR-1 likely because it is completely far sided from their POV. The source of this event is likely an eruption from beyond the STEREO A West limb, as field line opening and post eruptive arcades can be seen in this vicinity in STEREO A EUVI 195 beginning at approx. 2026-06-09T09:00Z. This CME is only visible for a few STEREO A COR2 frames due to its reduced campaign cadence.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A plane-of-sky using a longitude of W150.4 (STEREO is currently located at W60.4) due to source along STEREO A's West limb and lack of imagery to triangulate.

data.note: The source of this event is a filament eruption seen originating from the vicinity of Active Region 14463 (N17E15) beginning at approximately 2026-06-09T15:46Z. Filament material can be seen in SDO AIA, STEREO A EUVI and GOES SUVI 304. A wide region of dimming, field line opening and a slight EUV wave is also visible in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211, STEREO A EUVI 195 and GOES SUVI 284 appearing to exhibit heavy Eastern deflection, possibly due to the eruptions proximity to a coronal hole.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Wide CME first seen to the WNW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-06-09T21:12Z. It is also seen to the W in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1. The source of this CME is most likely wide moving field lines seen from beyond the W limb in GOES SUVI 284 beginning around 2026-06-09T20:36Z. Movement beyond the W limb is also seen in STEREO A EUVI 195 beginning as early as 2026-06-09T19:35Z. In coronagraphs, this CME partially overlaps with CME: 2026-06-09T21:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: A plane-of-sky measurement was chosen because the source is beyond the W limb but without visual confirmation of location of eruption.

data.note: CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-06-09T21:36Z. It is also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 but is covered by a real-time data gap in STEREO A COR2. The is most likely an eruption from AR 14461 (S21W19) that appears to be heavily deflected southward likely due its proximity to a coronal hole that was centered around N00W05. The eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 193 as moving field lines and a large area of dimming directed toward the south. The eruption is also accompanied by C2.3 class flare from AR 14461 that peaked at 2026-06-09T19:18Z best seen in SDO AIA 131. In coronagraphs, this CME partially overlaps with far-sided CME: 2026-06-09T21:12Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Speculative measurement based on the visible source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME first seen to the Northeast in SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-10T18:00Z, but the leading edge quickly fades before exiting the field-of-view in C2 and is therefore not clearly seen in other coronagraphs. The source of this event is field line opening seen from beyond the NE limb in GOES SUVI 284 beginning at approx. 2026-06-10T17:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using a longitude of E90 due to source near the limb and lack of coronagraph imagery to triangulate.

data.note: CME first seen to the NW in STEREO A COR2 beginning at 2026-06-10T18:08Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This event is obscured by the pylon in SOHO LASCO C3. The source of this CME is a filament eruption seen from beyond the West limb (approx. N15W150) in STEREO A EUVI 304 and 195 beginning at approx. 2026-06-10T17:25Z. The Solar Orbiter STIX instrument observed an estimated M7.0 [M3.9 - X1.3] peaking at 2026-06-10T17:17Z which may be related to this event. This CME overlaps with CME: 2026-06-10T18:12Z in STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME first seen to the South by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-10T18:12Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this CME is field line opening seen off the SW limb (approx. S25W150) in STEREO A EUVI 195 beginning at approx. 2026-06-10T17:35Z, indicating a far sided event. This CME overlaps with CME: 2026-06-10T18:08Z, which is also the result of an eruption from beyond the West limb in STEREO A, but is further North.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Bright loop CME and shock first seen to the Northeast by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-11T00:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this CME is a long duration C6.7 class flare from Active Region 14465 (N09E39) seen peaking at 2026-06-11T00:02Z. This flare can be seen in SDO AIA 131 along with a wide region of dimming, field line opening and an EUV wave seen in SDO AIA 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: UPDATED BULK parameters using later frames in SOHO LASCO C3 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

Updated shock measurement based on the best fit between the outermost wide feature seen in SOHO LASCO C3 imagery and a majority of the widest feature seen in STEREO A COR2 imagery, excluding small portions of the upper and lower sections of the shock feature.
PRELIMINARY BULK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.
PRELIMINARY SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR3 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: This CME is visible to the east/southeast in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 imagery. The source is an eruption and opening of field lines visible over the eastern limb in SDO AIA 171/193 and GOES SUVI 171/195 imagery starting around 2026-06-11T07:30Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on the best fit between SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2 imagery.

data.note: Faint, thin CME observed to the NE in SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2. The source is likely associated with a C9.0 flare (N10E34) from AR 14465 peaking at 2026-06-11T08:28Z, and a larger area of dimming centered nearby (N12E28) observed in SDO AIA 193 triggered with the flare.

cmeAnalyses.note: Triangulation between STEREO A COR2 which views the front better, and SOHO LASCO C2.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the E only in STEREO A COR2. The source is likely dimming in SDO AIA 193 starting around 2026-06-11T08:48Z centered around S25W32.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only 3D fit using the observed source centered at W32. The front is very faint and difficult to resolve even in running difference imagery, and parameters may vary as a result of this uncertainty, but it does evolve slowly regardless.

data.note: Faint CME observed to the E only in STEREO A COR2, likely due to being occulted by the GOES CCOR-1 and/or SOHO LASCO C2/C3 occulting disks, or missed by a SOHO LASCO C2/C3 downlink delay starting at 2026-06-11T19:36Z. The source may be AR 14465, as a weak filament eruption and field line movement centered around N08E33 is seen starting around 2026-06-11T17:04Z in SDO AIA 193.

cmeAnalyses.note: STEREO A COR2 only 3D analysis using E33 as the likely source longitude.

data.note: CME observed to the S in GOES CCOR-1 and SOHO LASCO C3, not in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap starting at 2026-06-11T19:53Z and not in SOHO LASCO C2 due to a downlink gap between approximately 2026-06-11T19:36Z to 2026-06-11T22:12Z. The source is a far-sided high southern latitude filament eruption observed in GOES SUVI 304 over the S limb at 2026-06-11T19:32Z and on/beyond the SW limb in STEREO A EUVI 304 at 2026-06-11T20:15Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: GOES CCOR-1 plane-of-sky with no STEREO A COR2 to triangulate the far-sided source.

data.note: Very narrow, minor CME seen to the southeast in SOHO LASCO, STEREO A COR2A, and GOES CCOR-1 without a very clear source; may be associated with a narrow eruption seen best in GOES SUVI 284 near 2026-06-12T00:30Z near the eastern limb, however, confidence is fairly low as the CME geometry would suggest a much further southerly latitude than this source.

cmeAnalyses.note: Preliminary leading edge measurement using all available spacecraft and triangulation to fit the source.

data.note: Narrow CME seen to the southeast in STEREO A COR2A and very dimly to the due south in SOHO LASCO C2 which is likely associated with an eruption with dimming from AR 14464 near S12W20 around 2026-06-12T13:50Z seen best in SDO AIA composite imagery using the sum of 211/193/171 Angstrom imagers. Also seen in STEREO A EUV 195 imagery.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using SOHO LASCO C2 and STEREO A COR2A for triangulation, noting the eastward deflection along the Earth-Sun line due to the presence of an equatorial coronal hole near W45.

data.note: Faint partial halo CME seen in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1 directed towards the east. The CME narrower with a brighter bulk and disconnected bulk/shock as seen in STEREO A COR2A, with a brighter bulk to the east-northeast and shock extending from the southeast to the north. This CME is associated with a filament eruption near N00E35 erupting near 2026-06-12T16:15Z, best seen in SDO AIA composite imagery using the sum of 211/193/171 Angstroms and as well in GOES SUVI/SDO AIA 304 Angstroms. This CME, seen due east and northeast in COR2A, is seen overlapping the previous CME: 2026-06-12T15:38Z which is seen to the southeast and which is a separate eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement out to 10 solar radii with medium confidence using SOHO/STEREO A/GOES for triangulation; the CME appears to fit closer to the Earth-Sun line than the source at E35 given the halo-like presentation.

data.note: Narrow CME first seen to the SSE by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-12T18:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a filament eruption likely originating from the far side seen in GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-06-12T18:16Z. Faint field line movement can also be seen along the SE limb in SDO AIA 171 in association with this eruption.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: Loop CME first seen to the East by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-12T19:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a filament eruption seen along the Eastern limb (approx. S10E80 with some Northern deflection) in SDO AIA /GOES SUVI 304 beginning at approx. 2026-06-12T18:56Z. Wide opening field lines and post eruptive arcades are also visible in SDO AIA 131, 171, 193, 211 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: BULK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.
SHOCK measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3 and GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME first seen to the East beginning at 2026-06-12T23:00Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. This CME is not seen in STEREO A COR2 due to a data gap beginning at 2026-06-12T20:23Z. The source of this event is likely continued outflow following a large filament eruption resulting in CME: 2026-06-12T19:24Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky using a longitude of E90 due to lack of clear source and no STEREO A COR2 imagery to triangulate.

data.note: Narrow, outflow CME first seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C2 starting at 2026-06-13T03:36Z. This feature is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-06-12T19:24Z as a separate source has not been found. It is also seen to the E in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based solely on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 as no source could be found.

data.note: Narrow CME first seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C2 starting around 2026-06-13T11:01Z. It is also seen to the SE in SOHO LASCO C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2. This CME is most likely far-sided as no source candidate was found on the Earth-facing disk. This is consistent with the triangulated measurement.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best-fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 stating at 2026-06-13T13:26Z. It is also seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C3 and GOES CCOR-1 and to the S in STEREO A COR2. The majority of this CME was missed by SOHO LASCO C2/C3 in real time due to a data gap between downlink periods. The source of this CME is a large eruption in across the far SE portion of the Earth-facing disk centered around AR 14461 (S21W68). The eruption is best seen in SDO AIA 193 as wide opening field lines accompanied by dimming and an EUVI wave beginning around 2026-06-13T12:36Z. This CME is also associated with a C2.5 class flare from AR 14461 which peaked at 2026-06-13T13:09Z. The flare is best seen in SDO AIA 131.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on best fit among SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1, and STEREO A COR2 as well as on visible source location.

data.note: Narrow, faint CME first seen to the SW in SOHO LASCO C2 around 2026-06-13T17:36Z. Not clearly visible in other coronagraph imagery. No source has been found on the Earth-facing disk. This feature is most likely outflow following CME: 2026-06-13T13:36Z.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement chosen because this feature is only seen in SOHO LASCO C2 and does not have a source candidate on the Earth-facing disk.

data.note: CME seen to the due north in SOHO LASCO C2 and GOES CCOR-1 in association with a far-sided eruption occurring near the solar north pole near 2026-06-14T19:00Z, best seen in GOES SUVI 284 as a fast loop with separating field lines over the limb.

cmeAnalyses.note: Leading edge measurement using primarily SOHO LASCO C2 and a few frames of GOES CCOR-1.

data.note: CME first seen to the Northeast by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-15T02:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3 in later frames. This CME is not clearly seen in STEREO A COR2 or GOES CCOR-1. The source of this event is likely far sided, as no clear on disk signatures are observed.

cmeAnalyses.note: Plane-of-sky measurement using a longitude of E90 due to far sided source and lack of coronagraph imagery to triangulate.

data.note: Bright loop CME first seen to the Southwest by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-15T06:36Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is a large, slow prominence eruption beginning at approx. 2026-06-15T03:00Z, with liftoff beginning at 2026-06-15T06:00Z as seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA and GOES SUVI 304. Field line opening can also be seen in SDO AIA 171, 193 and GOES SUVI 284.

cmeAnalyses.note: Measurement based on approximate source location and best fit in SOHO LASCO C2/C3, GOES CCOR-1 and STEREO A COR2.

data.note: Faint CME first seen to the Southwest by SOHO LASCO C2 beginning at 2026-06-15T07:24Z, as well as by SOHO LASCO C3, STEREO A COR2 and GOES CCOR-1 in later frames. The source of this event is faint field line opening seen along the SW limb in SDO AIA 171 in ISWA beginning at approx. 2026-06-15T07:00Z. This CME heavily overlaps with CME: 2026-06-15T06:36Z which is related to a large prominence eruption.
